title: AEP cross-skill vocabulary
description: The canonical declaration of every enumerated value more than one AEP skill reads or writes. Authored once in skills/product-context/_shared/references/ and materialized into each consuming skill by scripts/build-skills.sh, because the `skills` CLI installs one directory at a time and a validator cannot reach across install boundaries. Nothing validates against this document as a whole: consumers either load a named $def at runtime (coherence.mjs, derive.mjs) or declare a matching enum tagged with x-aep-vocab, which scripts/check-vocabulary.mjs proves identical. Adding a value here and nowhere else is the intended workflow — a half-applied taxonomy change is this repo's #1 bug class.

story_status.title: Story lifecycle state
story_status.description: product-context.yaml stories[].status. Five stages on the normal path plus three exceptions that wait on a human. Written by /aep-dispatch (ready → in_progress), /aep-wrap (→ completed / failed, and pending → ready once dependencies complete), and a human (failed → pending is the one transition no agent may make).

x-aep-stages.pending: dependencies unmet or not yet dispatched
x-aep-stages.in_progress: a workspace agent is building it
x-aep-stages.blocked: a dependency failed — waits on a human
x-aep-stages.failed: retries exhausted — only a human may reset it to pending

story_status_signal.title: Story state a workspace may report
story_status_signal.description: The subset of story_status a workspace agent writes into .dev-workflow/signals/status.json. A workspace never reports pending, ready, blocked, or deferred: those are control-plane states owned by the main session, and a workspace that claims one is reporting on work it does not own.

layer_gate_status.title: Layer gate state
layer_gate_status.description: product-context.yaml layer_gates[].status. Two-phase and coverage-checked: scripted_passed means the layer's Tier-1 suite is green (machinery proven, live product not yet); passed additionally requires every applicable higher tier green, every acceptance criterion covered, and prior-layer journeys replaying green. /aep-dispatch refuses to start layer N while layer N-1 is anything other than passed — scripted_passed still blocks.

x-aep-stages.running: a gate run is in flight
x-aep-stages.scripted_passed: Tier-1 green; higher tiers or coverage still pending
x-aep-stages.passed: all applicable tiers green + coverage complete + regression replay green
x-aep-stages.failed: a gate run failed on product behavior (distinct from a preflight REFUSING on environment)
x-aep-stages.deferred: gate execution postponed by a human
x-aep-stages.waived: a human accepted the layer without the full gate, on the record

dogfood_target.title: What Tier-2 journeys run against
dogfood_target.description: skills/e2e-test/policy.md dogfood_target — the surface and environment, not the tool. none is reserved for a repo with no runnable surface at all (pure config / schema / docs), where Tier 2 is N/A and there is no journeys/ dir.

oneOf.description: deployed:<url> — a deployed environment, typically reached after merge → deploy

x-aep-stages.none: no runnable surface (config / schema / docs repo)
x-aep-stages.cli: the built command-line binary, driven by bash

journey_target_type.title: Journey surface type
journey_target_type.description: A journey's target: — resolves which TOOL executes it (browser/device driver vs bash), where dogfood_target resolves the surface and environment. A target: web journey on a dogfood_target: cli project is a scaffolding error, not a preference.

journey_timing.title: When a journey is executed
journey_timing.description: skills/e2e-test/policy.md journey_timing. Governs EXECUTION only, never authoring: the journey file is always a pre-merge /aep-build Phase 6 deliverable. Under post-deploy a merge sits at scripted_passed until the deployed dogfood flips it to passed.

verification_tier.title: How much verification this story earns
verification_tier.description: Derived into verification-recipe.json and published on status.json at Phase 5 entry. light scores no dimensions (structured self-review); standard runs the derived preset; deep runs it with nothing de-weighted and, where a second model family is available, prefers a different family from the generator. Canonical treatment: /aep-gen-eval → references/verification-economics.md.

failure_class.title: What kind of failure a FAIL is
failure_class.description: Assigned per finding, mandatory at every FAIL before a recovery rung is chosen — status.json is the autopilot's only workspace input, so a FAIL published without a class cannot be routed. Routing is conjunctive: every non-zero class routes and none masks another. Only product-defect climbs the recovery ladder.

x-aep-stages.product-defect: the built thing is wrong — finding → story / fix commit → gen-eval
x-aep-stages.environment: an unmet precondition outside the product (credential, access, unseeded target) — the ops / environment_repair path, re-probed each tick
x-aep-stages.harness-flake: the verification apparatus failed, not the product — quarantine and re-run after ratification
x-aep-stages.scope: the spec and the work disagree — the human gate

error_class.title: Execution mechanics of a build/CI failure
error_class.description: The pre-existing enum on status.json failure logs, recording HOW a run died. It stays; failure_class is the routing layer above it, defaulting per the error_class → failure_class mapping in verification-economics.md.

e2e_tier.title: Verification tier
e2e_tier.description: Which tiers gate a layer is per-project (skills/e2e-test/policy.md). A CLI or library is 1 + 2, an API service 1 + 3, a web/mobile app 1 + 2 (+ 3); only a repo with no runnable surface is 1-only.

x-aep-stages.1: Scripted gates — proves the MACHINERY, in the project's own test framework
x-aep-stages.2: Journey dogfood — proves the PRODUCT against real providers/env, from skills/e2e-test/journeys/
x-aep-stages.3: API drivers — backend state, bulk setup, async flows, via throwaway scripts in .dev-workflow/
